chapter: Western University and Kansas City nightlife
title: Lester Young's and Ben Webster's styles in 1933, Dick Wilson
summary: Lester's spacey tenor, Ben not yet formed, Ellington bringing it out, and Dick Wilson as local contender.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: That's right. But what I was getting at was in '33, how well were the styles of Lester Young and Ben Webster developed?

Well, Lester had a very spacey sound. In fact, I still kinda' try to play like that now. He would play a phrase and maybe lay out three beats before he'd come in with another phrase. You know, 'stead of more continuous staying on style, like Bird would play, you know.
Yeah.
He plays, "Bop-pe-ba-pe-doom-bop-be-dum, bip-bip-dum-boh-bop-pe-bop-pe-dip-bop," you know.
Yes.
That sort of thing.
Spacey is a good word for that.

Yeah. He had kinda loosened up. Now Ben Webster had not developed that style at all. In fact, I don't even think that he had developed it when he was with Teddy Wilson. I think Duke Ellington brought that out of Ben.
Well, look, I mean, once you do it==
He and Johnny Hodges and those guys --
Well, Johnny influenced him, he always said that he did.
Yeah. Plus you could see that Ben found himself, seemed to me, like, in that.

But when you hear Ben on the records with Bennie Moten, and then you hear him with -- well, he did record with Duke once in the '30s, and then again--It wasn't until with Duke that he's really impressive--
Yeah.
--as compared with the others.
Yeah. Well, they were busy running, but I would say that at that time, everybody kinda' thought that Dick Wilson was next for President in Kansas City.
Yeah.
And the three of them were battles whenever the bands were in town, you know.
Dick Wilson was technically a pretty good musician, wasn't he?
I didn't know that much of him, you know, I didn't get to know him too--
Sounds as though he's got a good talent.
Yeah. One thing I do remember might've been the thing that they held against him. He liked to play lots a' high, screaming notes--not as high as Jackie but --
Oh, did he?
--he liked to play lots of the higher parts of the saxophone, you know.
Oh.
But he--
